## Summary

The 2025 Irish presidential election took place on Friday, 24 October 2025. Note that the election occurred in October, not November.

**Results:**

Catherine Connolly, an independent candidate, won with 63.4% of votes, defeating Fine Gael's Heather Humphreys who received 29.5%, and Fianna Fáil's Jim Gavin who got 7.2%. 

Connolly, a pro-immigration self-avowed socialist, won the election in a landslide. Her inauguration is scheduled for November 2025 at Dublin Castle.

The Irish presidential election took place on October 24, 2025, and Catherine Connolly was elected on the first count, winning 914,143 first-preference votes.

The winner was independent TD and former Leas-Cheann Comhairle, Catherine Connolly, representing the left/progressive wing. Humphreys, who won 29.46 per cent of first preference votes, has congratulated Connolly on becoming "a president for all of us", and a third candidate on the ballot, the Fianna Fail-backed Jim Gavin, withdrew from the race earlier in October following a controversy over a rental dispute.

The inauguration of the new President is scheduled for November 2025 at Dublin Castle.
